# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: SW-APT-01 (Simulated)
- Period: week 11 (starting 2026-03-16)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift found that this clinic's scans no longer resemble the scans on which the AI was validated (drift score 1.00, where 0.5 indicates similarity to training data and 1 indicates a clear difference). 

Consequently, the catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) cannot be verified from the 50 scans from this week, and expert grades for these scans have not yet been received. The AI is referring more patients than usual, accounting for 90% of this week's scans, compared with 68% of the training scans.

## 4. Potential patient impact
As the catch rate cannot be verified, the number of possibly missed cases is not estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
Significant degradation in image quality, resolution, brightness, and sharpness compared with the training data, accompanied by a drift score of 1.00. (Category: camera or image quality; confidence 95%; source: gemini)

Evidence:
- Drift score is 1.00, indicating scans do not resemble training data
- Mean resolution decreased from 1020.0 px to 224.0 px (relative change -0.781)
- Mean quality dropped from 0.5 to 0.113 (relative change -0.773)
- Mean sharpness dropped from 0.000399 to 7.53e-05 (relative change -0.811)
- Mean contrast decreased from 0.0963 to 0.0655 (relative change -0.32)
- Mean brightness decreased from 0.373 to 0.315 (relative change -0.155)
- Referral rate increased from 0.685 to 0.9 (relative change 0.315)

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift paused the AI at this clinic because the scans have drifted beyond the data on which the AI was validated, meaning the catch rate cannot be verified. We recommend sending this clinic's scans for human grading until the checks below are complete.

Checks:
- [ ] Inspect the camera hardware and clean the lens optics
- [ ] Verify camera export settings to ensure resolution has not been inadvertently downscaled
- [ ] Check ambient lighting and flash intensity settings on the imaging device

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm forms part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response must fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
